The presentation explores the causes and cures for interference in multilingual translation models. Many methods have been proposed to alleviate interference, often demonstrated using small models, but they do not always work better than a tuned baseline. The work focuses on identifying the main factors contributing to interference or synergy, finding that severe interference happens when the model is small relative to the data size. The presentation also looks at what factors influence the loss for a language pair in bilingual and multilingual MT, including model size, data size, the data size of other languages, language similarity, and the number of languages. It concludes that language similarity is not a dominant factor for interference and that severe interference occurs in parameter poverty settings. The presenter suggests that temperature sampling can be a key factor for strong baselines.

The paper presents MultiEMO, a multimodal fusion framework for emotion recognition in conversations, which outperforms existing methods on two ERC benchmark datasets, MELD and IEMOCAP.
